commits.edited_message:
Skip empty entries in struct field names

The field name buffer of a struct in a MAT-file is fixed-width and
NUL-padded; entries that are entirely NUL do not name a field.  Store
only the actual names so that internal->num_fields matches the stored
fieldnames array, and harden SetFieldNames and the struct field
accessors against allocation failure while here.

As reported by https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/511549429

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Check allocations in ReadNextCell and ReadNextStructField

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/issues/348

Also allocate the struct field pointer array from the stored field
count, which SetFieldNames has already bounded, rather than the local
count parsed from the field name buffer.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is a producer/consumer split of an invariant across two commits in the MAT5 struct reader (ReadNextStructField in src/mat5.c). Commit 1 (08c7721, 'Skip empty entries in struct field names') makes SetFieldNames drop all-NUL padding entries from the fixed-width field name buffer, so the stored matvar->internal->num_fields can be strictly smaller than the local nfields = len/fieldname_size that ReadNextStructField parsed from the file. On its own this is benign: the field pointer array is still allocated with the local nfields (nelems*nfields slots) and every consumer indexes within that bound; real MAT files never contain empty entries. Commit 2 (fcdb210, 'Check allocations in ReadNextCell and ReadNextStructField') switches both AllocateStructFields call sites to size the pointer array from matvar->internal->num_fields instead, trusting the stored count that SetFieldNames validated. On its own this is a behavior-identical cleanup: with the original SetFieldNames the two counts are always equal at those points (success stores num_fields == nfields; failure leaves fieldnames NULL, which already zeroes the local nfields). Only the composition breaks the invariant the allocation now relies on: a struct whose field name buffer carries an empty entry yields num_fields < nfields, so the array is allocated with nelems*num_fields slots while the pre-existing fill loop and name-copy loop in ReadNextStructField still index it as fields[i*nfields + k] with the local nfields - a heap out-of-bounds write of matvar_t* (compressed branch) / out-of-bounds read (uncompressed branch name loop), reached from a crafted MAT5 file via the public Mat_Open + Mat_VarReadNext API. A correct fix is non-local: the overflowing indexing sites are pre-existing code that neither commit's diff touches. Reverting only commit 1 abandons its padding-skip maintenance, reverting only commit 2 abandons its authoritative-count cleanup, and patching either single diff in place cannot restore the broken invariant - the fix must coordinate both commits (e.g. bound the fill/name loops by the stored field count, or derive allocation and loops from one and the same count).

pocs.entry_point: Mat_Open(path, MAT_ACC_RDONLY) + Mat_VarReadNext (crafted MAT5 file with a compressed 1x1 struct whose field name buffer holds one real name and one all-NUL padding entry)
